subject: Intermittent degradation carveout & tiered monthly credit scheme (exception request)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hexagontech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@hexagontech.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exception request: intermittent degradation carveout & credits

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we start load testing our batched inference pipelines were seeing predictable short-duration degradations during heavy nightly windows (typically 03:00-05:30 PT) while jobs drain and re-batch. Our SREs want to avoid a hard SLA breach for the first 3 months of production while we optimize prefixes and caching.

Specifically we're asking:
- A temporary carveout that treats degradations under 30 minutes per calendar day (during scheduled drain window) as non-breach for the first 90 days post-launch.
- A modified monthly credit calculation for that period: instead of immediate pro-rata credits, hold back up to 50% of any credits and reconcile after 90 days based on observed reduction in incidents.

We appreciate Redwoods standard 99.95% uptime target and understand this is exceptional. This is about avoiding noisy SLA churn while we stabilize. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Offer a provisional waiver for the first 3 months tied to specific maintenance windows?
2) Accept a holdback/reconciliation model for credits (holdback then true-up)?

Attached is our short questionnaire and some traces that show the pattern.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering, HexagonTech
[Attachment: Hexagon_SLA_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hexagontech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: intermittent degradation carveout & credits

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the traces. I looped in Laura (enterprise contracts) and Ben (reliability/sla policies) to make sure we cover both legal and operational considerations. High level: were open to a limited, conditional approach but need to align on measurable guardrails. Preliminary thoughts:

- Scope & duration:
  - Provisional waiver period: 90 days from production cutover, tied only to the nightly drain window you specified (03:00-05:30 PT). Outside of that window normal SLA applies.

- Incident qualification:
  - Degradation must be captured by our latency/availability signals and cross-validated by your ops traces. We propose a joint signal threshold (p95 latency > X ms AND 5% request failure rate) to count an event. Events under 30 minutes/day within the window would be excluded from the uptime calculation during the waiver.

- Credit holdback & reconciliation:
  - For months 1-3, Redwood would hold back up to 50% of calculated monthly credits (maximum holdback cap = 1x monthly spend) into a reconciliation escrow.
  - At day 91 we run a joint review. If the event rate decreases by >= 60% vs month 1 baseline, held credits are forfeit (no payout). Otherwise, credits are released pro-rata back to HexagonTech for the waiver period.

- Monitoring & transparency:
  - Well provide a dedicated dashboard and enable cross-account trace access for the waiver period to make reconciliations straightforward.

- Optional protections for Redwood:
  - If incidents persist beyond 3 months without measurable improvement, Redwood reserves the right to revoke waiver and default to standard credits.

Ill attach a short draft that reflects the above so Laura can translate into contract language. Can you confirm youre comfortable with: (a) the joint signal thresholds, and (b) the 60% improvement target for forfeit?

Next steps: Laura will prepare a provisional waiver draft (no legal binding right now) and we can iterate.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: provisional_waiver_draft_v2.docx]

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hexagontech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@hexagontech.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: intermittent degradation carveout & credits

Mina —

Appreciate the quick and thoughtful reply. A few clarifying points from our SRE lead:

- Joint signal thresholds: happy to align — suggest p95 > 450ms AND error rate >= 4% to avoid capturing routine GC spikes. Well provide traces to calibrate exact numbers before cutover.

- Improvement target: 60% is reasonable but can we add an intermediate checkpoint at day 45 for a partial release (25% of held credits) if we see steady progress? That would help our finance team manage burn.

- Holdback cap: 1x monthly spend is OK but would you consider a hard absolute cap of $150k for month 1 to avoid surprise exposure? We can model both ways.

Were aligned on the monitoring dashboard — please include read access for our SREs. If Laura can send a draft today well review and route it internally.

Thanks,
Daniel

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@hexagontech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: intermittent degradation carveout & credits

Daniel —

Thanks, that feedback is helpful and practical. Well incorporate the changes:

- Thresholds: well mark the thresholds as "calibration variables" in the waiver (placeholder: p95 450ms / error >=4%) and run a 7-day tuning window pre-cutover to lock values.
- Midpoint release: add day-45 checkpoint for a 25% automatic release of held credits if improvement trend is positive (defined as monotonic month-over-month reduction and no more than 1 qualifying incident in the 7 days prior to checkpoint).
- Hard cap: Redwood agrees to an absolute holdback cap of $150,000 for month 1 only. Monthly cap thereafter reverts to min(1x monthly spend, $150k).

Laura will push a provisional waiver draft to the HubSpot link and cc you. Ben will set up a shared dashboard with read-only access for HexagonTech SREs.

Action items:
- Laura: circulate draft waiver + redlines link (today).
- Ben: enable dashboard + pre-cutover 7-day calibration window.
- Daniel: confirm cutover date so we can schedule calibration.

Ill mark this as a provisional exception and queue it for legal review after your sign-off on technical metrics.

Best,
Mina
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
